description: The bar chart illustrates performance comparisons across various large language models (LLMs) on two benchmark datasets—MATH-500 and AIME24—grouped into six subplots (a–f), each representing different model scales or configurations. The horizontal axis in each subplot categorizes models by parameter size (e.g., 3B, 1.5B, 7B, 671B) or “unk” (unknown or unspecified scale), while the vertical axis represents performance score, ranging from 65 to 100 for MATH-500 and 0 to 90 for AIME24, with tick marks at intervals of 5 or 10. Each bar is color- and pattern-coded according to the model type, as indicated in the legend: CoT (white), Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct (blue hatched), Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct (green solid), o1-mini (pink solid), DeepSeek-R1 (yellow solid), o1 (gray solid), TTS (white with black outline), GPT-4o (purple solid), o1-preview (brown solid), and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-7B (orange hatched). In subplot (a) for MATH-500, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct (78.2) outperforms GPT-4o (74.6) and Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct (71.4). In (b), o1-mini (90.0) and o1-preview (85.5) score highly, while in (c), DeepSeek-R1 (97.3), DeepSeek-R1-Distill-7B (95.2), and o1 (94.8) achieve top scores. For AIME24, subplot (d) shows Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct (30.0) and Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct (23.3) underperforming compared to o1-preview (9.3). In (e), o1-mini (63.6) and o1-preview (63.3) are comparable, while in (f), DeepSeek-R1-Distill-7B (83.3), DeepSeek-R1 (79.8), and o1 (79.2) lead. The chart visually supports the paper’s theme by showing that smaller models (e.g., 1.5B–7B) can rival or surpass larger models (e.g., 405B–671B) under certain scaling or inference strategies, particularly in MATH-500, while AIME24 shows more variability, with the largest models still dominating in (f).
